speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It has been a long day and I wish I could bring a song and dance item to break up the monotony of today's proceedings but that would not be allowed although I am sure it will be very welcome by Members of this House.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: People were confined to their homes, separated from loved ones, deprived of their usual social activities and anxious about the future.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: After ensuring that we had enough food and essential items, our next instinct was to seek comfort in anything that could provide a semblance of normalcy, many of us turned to Netflix and YouTube, re-watched old films.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We saw the videos on social media of people in other countries, singing, dancing, playing instruments and performing on their balconies to provide solace and companionship to their neighbours.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure many in this House were too.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: As the months dragged out, people sought ways to connect with others, to satisfy the need for human connection that we as human beings fundamentally need.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In our lowest moments, as the number of COVID-19 cases climbed higher, many of us felt powerless.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The arts helped keep us sane, helped us process our confusion and grief and entertained us, lifting our spirits.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: During the circuit breaker there was the poll in the newspapers reporting that Singaporeans thought artists had the most non-essential jobs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I was saddened to see that and felt it was unnecessary to include that poll of “non-essential jobs” at all.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps the arts have grown so commonplace and ingrained in our lives that we started taking it for granted.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The arts have contributed not just in terms of providing comfort and strength during difficult times, but also to our economy.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: There was a time when the arts held a great deal of importance to our society and our leaders.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: From former Acting Minister for Culture Mr Ong Teng Cheong who first recognised the importance of arts institutions in Singapore and who created what is now the National Arts Council, to former Minister of Information and the Arts, Mr George Yeo who aimed to turn Singapore into a culturally attractive global city through the Global City for the Arts project, we once saw the arts as a viable and important part of city-planning and development for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, it seems that the arts have fallen from their previous stature.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Artists today are struggling and many live hand-to-mouth.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This past month, I spoke with Edward, a 23-year-old Nee Soon South resident and professional actor, singer and dancer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Despite having a diploma in performance, he makes $10,000 a year, less than $1,000 a month, through his various freelance gigs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Edward worries about the future, specifically to what extent he will be able to support himself through his profession and whether he will ever be able to afford the expenses of starting a family.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: When the circuit breaker measures were announced, all of the jobs Edward had signed on for evaporated, leaving him with very zero income.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: He is now returning to school to "upskill" and shared with me about his worries – whether there will be any opportunities left available for him in the arts sector when he re-enters the workforce in a few years.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Although permanent casuals might work full-time or part-time, they are paid hourly with no health or leave benefits.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Such workers do not benefit from the Job Support Scheme or JSS because they are only paid for their time and therefore have no regular pay from their companies to begin with.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They also do not qualify for the Self-employed Persons Relief Scheme because they typically often work exclusively for one company.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: From January 2021 onwards, JSS support will be reduced to 0%.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: There is a real risk that people like Edward may not have opportunities to return to, if or when the sector does recover.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Lack of stable income, heightened by COVID-19 restrictions, are forcing arts workers to seek other jobs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The arts and entertainment sector is incredibly diverse.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is not just made up of writers, actors, musicians and poets.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It also includes lighting and sound technicians, school CCA teachers, museum operators, fashion designers, event photographers, and many more highly skilled people who produce and enable the productions that we consume.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If we continue to do nothing more for them in terms of financial support during this time, they may be lost to other sectors, to the long-term detriment of our arts and entertainment industry.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: An entire sector may be at risk of being wiped out.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I was disappointed that in yesterday's Ministerial Statement by the Deputy Prime Minister, there was no mention of any extension of support to the arts sector workers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: To be fair to the Government, the $55 million Arts and Culture Resilience Package is certainly helpful, but it can be enhanced to make the support accessible for all arts workers, including permanent casuals.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Granted, NAC and IMDA may be approaching these funding criteria with consumer perspective and safety in mind, but I urge consideration on the limitations to creativity and marketability of our arts productions if only G-rated productions can receive funding.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Parental controls on online media platforms exist for a reason, for parents to be involved and exercise the necessary control over children's media consumption.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This should not be a responsibility that is shifted over to the state, with costs that the arts and entertainment sector ends up bearing, to the detriment of an industry's vibrancy and sustainability.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If we invest in its development and the development of those who are keen to have a career in the arts, it can provide financial upliftment to individuals and families.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Take the story of another resident Yusri better known Shaggy in this industry.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Despite being from a low-income and challenged family, he made a career and eventually a business out of being an arts technician and multimedia designer for stage productions.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: He saw the arts as a way out of poverty and it has, so far.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: His work in the arts provided him with a better life than he had when he was growing up.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Yusri is quite established now in his livelihood after spending more than 10 years in the sector.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: He was also personally also highly resourceful in seeking out courses in business and marketing that could help his arts career.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the progress thus far, Yusri sees such opportunities disappearing for those starting in the industry today like Edward.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Where in the past it was not necessary to have a degree to begin work in the arts and entertainment sector, it is now increasingly important, despite wages staying the same.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: He also shares the same anxieties about the future as Edward.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The arts and entertainment industry is one that has tremendous potential and unlimited in its "export capacity" – thanks to technology and the Internet.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Besides being now known globally, Korean entertainment has created subsequent demand worldwide for Korean-branded merchandise including cosmetics and food.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Even the example of a local food establishment cited by Deputy Prime Minister Heng yesterday during his speech – Seonggong, is also a Korean brand.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This is the result of active and committed investment by the Korean government since the 1960s, in preserving traditional and modern culture, and actively promoting it internationally.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore can emulate Korea's example, and go even further, potentially increasing our soft power internationally as well.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the Government will consider investing more into the development of the arts.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Create business mentorship and marketing training specifically for artists and entertainers so that they can acquire business literacy to make better livelihoods out of their talent and craft.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The arts and entertainment sector can also benefit from professionalisation such as a wage framework guideline so that artists are not subject to the devaluation of their work and a race to the bottom to get jobs, which is happening often currently.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In our Future Economy deliberations, I sincerely hope the arts and entertainment sector will receive due consideration for its potential.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: When I was 16 years old, I told my parents I would like to study fashion design and become a fashion designer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They told me I would not be able to make a decent living out of it, and insisted I get a degree in NUS which I did.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am sad to observe that 20 years on, this still rings true.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The Singapore Tourism Board marketed us as a country where "passion is made possible".

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It was a wonderful campaign, but such efforts should go beyond being a short-term marketing campaign.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We need broad and deep capacity-building, for the diverse talents and passion for our people to thrive.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: To summarise, I have four specific proposals for the House to consider and to support.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Three, to develop a wage guideline framework for the arts sector, in consultation with the sector's workers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And lastly, to invest in capacity-building of the arts and entertainment sector through overseas exchanges, scholarships, as well as business and marketing training for arts and media students, artists and arts producers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In the 1930s in America, Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal included a "Federal One" project.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The federal government hired more than 10,000 artists to create works of art across the country, including murals, theatre, fine arts, music, writing, design, and so on.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It was part of a plan to stimulate economic recovery during the Great Depression, where there was widespread poverty and high unemployment.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This plan helped put artists back to work on lifting the spirits of a people, and inspiring them towards a more hopeful future amidst the economic turmoil of that time.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We could take a leaf out of that book.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Art can be a great nation-building tool, forging common identity amongst the people amidst a crisis.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And what do we envision when we say "Singapore Together"?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like Ms Carrie Tan, MCCY recognises that our arts and culture play a critical role in our efforts to foster a more caring people, cohesive society and nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The arts play a key role in connecting different communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The arts show the world who we are and what we stand for, as a people and as a nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During these unprecedented times, the arts and culture sector is even more essential than ever, as a source of inspiration and hope for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Ms Carrie Tan noted, the Government has since the 1980s, initiated deep seated efforts to develop a vibrant and sustainable arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Wide-ranging in breadth and aims, the Masterplans from the 1980s to the 2000s, such as the report of the Advisory Council on Culture and the Arts or ACCA, and the Renaissance City Plans have built a foundation for the growth of Singapore's art and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since 2012, our approach has been guided by the Arts and Culture Strategic Review or ACSR which seeks to bring arts and culture to everyone, everywhere, every day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This blueprint to enhance our arts and culture has made steady progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the Committee of Supply debate last year, MCCY noted that several ACSR outcomes, such as the number of arts and heritage activities have been registering healthy increases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The diversity and the types of activities, as well as attendance, have grown as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Despite such progress, we cannot rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY recognises the need to update our strategies and approaches, so that our arts and culture continue to strengthen Singapore's social fabric and unity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2018, these important aims were reflected in the inaugural Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans introduced after extensive engagement with stakeholders across the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These plans cover a span of five years until 2022, and comprehensively set out the strategies that will provide strong foundations on the continued growth of the arts and heritage sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These included the continued emphasis on nurturing arts excellence and focus on leveraging technology, that the Member spoke about as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Out of the eight strategic priorities in OurSgArts Plan includes addressing the needs of arts freelancers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To better support the development of our arts and culture, the Government has steadily and consistently increased funding for these sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Rolled out in 2014, the CMF matches qualifying donations raised by the arts and heritage groups dollar-for-dollar.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This has helped over 100 arts and heritage groups double their donation income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The grant has enabled these arts and heritage groups to develop their capabilities – this topic is also one of the four recommendations that she has talked about – for the long-term sustainability of the organisations as well as support digital productions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has, through its special budgets, released specific help and measures to boost incomes and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Arts organisations and practitioners are able to tap on broad-based measures such as the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS, Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme or SIRS, COVID-19 Support Grant or CSG and SEP Training Support Scheme for income support and skills training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government recognises that the arts and culture sector, like the retail and food industries, has been significantly affected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Hence, the sector will continue to receive further Government support till March year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is unlike what Ms Tan had suggested – that the arts and entertainment sector only receives 10% wage support under the JSS, with this dropping to 0% from January 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These organisations will receive a rate of 30% for seven more months, with disbursements in March and June 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I hope Ms Tan will be happy to hear this information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to these measures, MCCY also announced a $55 million Arts and Culture Resilience Package or ACRP in April 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The ACRP provides additional support and opportunities for the arts and culture community while encouraging the development of longer term capabilities that will help the sector emerge stronger after COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As announced on 21 August this year, MCCY will be providing an additional operating grant under the ACRP to support arts and culture organisations as well as those in closely related sectors that Ms Tan talked about earlier and that are key to the arts and culture eco-system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Ms Tan that we will announce additional details soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that the pandemic has disrupted livelihoods and plans in the arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Arts workers, including freelancers, have been hard hit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise the diverse capabilities of our arts and culture freelancers and how they contribute richly to our arts and culture eco-system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is important to provide them with ways and means to continue contributing in this sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY and NAC are working closely with partners to provide a range of support to boost the livelihoods and capabilities of freelancers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Allow me, Mdm Deputy Speaker, to share several ways in which MCCY and NAC are ramping up assistance and opportunities for the arts and culture sector, including freelancers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Capability development is also a topic that Ms Tan spoke passionately about in her speech earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Capability development has been and continues to be a long-standing priority for the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of the training programmes identified by the NAC are not only useful in raising the capabilities of arts freelancers across diverse domains, the programmes are also eligible under the SkillsFuture framework for costs to be defrayed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This supports ground-up efforts by artists and arts groups to present their work in digital form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This not only generates work opportunities, it also builds industry capabilities in digital content production.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Carrie Tan had noted that the DPG only supported productions rated General.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The DPG is created as a scheme during COVID-19 to support the efforts of artists and arts organisations wanting to present their work digitally or via a digital medium.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Unlike live performances which are subject to classification ratings under IMDA, online content, like she mentioned earlier, is easily and generally available with no age segregation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This makes it prudent for the DPG to underwrite productions rated General.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The DPG also serves to cater for inclusive access by all audiences, including young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I think a lot of Members in the room are parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to be there with our kids when they are consuming digital content but we cannot be certain that we will always be there guiding them when they are watching and consuming digital content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Hence, the DPG has supported a large number of digital works suitable for the general public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That being said, I want to assure Ms Carrie Tan that productions with a higher than General rating are still being supported.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Apart from the DPG, NAC has continued to provide funding for major companies, key arts groups and artists through NAC's regular grant schemes and commissions, which have been enhanced to include digital works and presentations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These could cover wide-ranging works, including those with a higher than General rating.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Thirdly, even though the arts and culture sector may be disrupted, practitioners in this sector continue to benefit from commissioned work and partnerships for key festivals and events like Silver Arts, Singapore Heritage Festival, Singapore Writers Festival and Singapore Art Week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: By end August, Mdm Deputy Speaker, 72 commissions and partnerships were supported under the ACRP, providing over 950 work opportunities, most of which were for freelancers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, NAC digitally adapted four performances for Silver Arts 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I think many of the Members in the Chamber, I think you have seen some of these productions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They have gone out to many of your elderly residents who usually will be out and about but they can now enjoy this programme in the safety of their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These were new works by Toy Factory, Asian Cultural Symphonic Orchestra, Wadah Seni Entertainment and Ding Yi Music Company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Their productions anchored the digital festival in September 2020 – just last month – and encouraged many of our seniors to stay engaged creatively through performances and activities in the comfort and in the safety of their homes – in fact, through their mobile devices, at their fingertips, through their mobile devices, anytime, anywhere.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another key project commissioned by the NAC was "Streets of Hope", which was an out-of-house and digital integrated campaign featuring original artworks at areas such as the civic district and presented digitally on the Gillman Barracks website and social media channels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Fourthly, Ms Tan raised the issue of "permanent casuals", or arts workers who may have neither benefited from JSS or SIRS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY recognises that these workers have critical skills and are valuable members of the arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have been working with our cultural institutions, including the Esplanade and Arts House Limited, to help workers engaged by these institutions apply for Government support schemes they are eligible for, including SIRS and also CSG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These institutions also provide the workers with information on job opportunities, including those under SGUnited Jobs initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We know it is not easy and our arts and culture workers, especially the freelancers, need all the help they can get.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The ARH, which was started in September 2019, has been engaging its stakeholders throughout this year to better understand their concerns during COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, NAC is working with partners from the arts community on initiatives to boost the industry, such as the one led by the artistic director of Drama Box, former Nominated Member of Parliament, Mr Kok Heng Leun, to look into best practices in the theatre scene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This effort will lead to recommendations on what constitutes good employment and fair work practices that can be adopted by both freelancers and companies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is an important topic, please allow me two more minutes to wrap up.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: You have to wrap up in one minute.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, Madam, in conclusion, let us continue to work closely together.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.
